transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02
Start: 10:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Nimbus, ML Eng), Aisha Khan (Nimbus, Head of ML), Samir Patel (Nimbus, Infra), Mei Wong (Nimbus, PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, hope you're all doing well. Quick agenda, we'll run through the latest benchmark sheet, talk about quality impact across int8 and fp8, discuss perf deltas and next steps. Priya's got the deep numbers.
[00:18] Carlos: Hey — yeah thanks, Jordan. We pushed new test harness overnight, used the 3 prompt sets we talked about.
[00:25] Priya: Cool, I have the numbers, I'll share my screen after. FYI some of the names in the sheet are a bit messy, I see K-V cache sometimes spelled K-V cash by the auto-transcriber so ignore that.
[00:40] Aisha: Thanks, quick ask: we need to know if the quality drop on INT8 is within our tolerances for downstream LLM QA.
[00:47] Jordan: Totally. Priya will run the diff and we'll flag any prompts that degrade beyond your threshold.

[02:05] Priya: OK jumping in. Summary first — on FP16 baseline we used Redwood-hosted baseline on g4-like instances sim for parity. INT8 reduced model size by about 2.9x and improved raw throughput 2.3x. FP8 gives slightly better latency than INT8 on short contexts but FP8 is not as mature on our runtime, we saw more kernel fallbacks in a few sequences.
[02:35] Samir: When you say kernel fallback, is that the runtime choosing a non-quantized path?
[02:40] Priya: Exactly, sometimes the compiler detects numerics that we mark as unsafe for the fast quantized kernel and falls back to mixed-precision, so the perf benefits drop for those sequences.

[04:00] Carlos: On quality numbers — we ran BLEU-style scoring for our templated prompts and an embedding-similarity metric for open prompts. Across 3 prompt sets INT8 had a mean delta of -1.8 BLEU points vs FP16; FP8 was -0.7 on the same sets. But variance matters: a small subset of prompts (about ~6%) showed bigger deltas up to -6 BLEU.
[04:34] Aisha: That 6% is concerning if it's customer-facing. Do we have examples?
[04:40] Priya: Yes I highlighted 5 prompts in the sheet — they're mostly long-context troubleshooting dialogues where KV cache interactions are heavy. INT8 seems to lose some subtle coherence there.

[06:00] Jordan: Let's be clear on the ask — Nimbus wants to push to production if average quality stays within X and tail cases are manageable with a fallback. Is that right, Aisha?
[06:12] Aisha: Yes, we can accept a small average degradation if we have deterministic fallbacks for the tail and if cost savings are substantial. Also need SOC 2/ISO notes and audit logs before we go to dedicated.

[07:00] Priya: On perf deltas, here's a quick table from the sheet — FP16 baseline QPS X, INT8 QPS ~2.3x, FP8 QPS ~1.9x on long sequences but FP8 had better p50 and p95 on short sequences. The 95th-percentile for INT8 increased a bit due to the fallback cases.
[07:28] Samir: Can you share the raw logs? We want to see tail latency distribution and any GPU utilization spikes.
[07:33] Priya: Will upload full logs to the shared drive (link in notes). Some of the 95p spikes correlate with model loading and repeated KV cache rewrites.

[09:00] Carlos: Did you run on dedicated pool or hosted? Because network hops matter for 95p.
[09:05] Priya: These specific runs were on hosted infra sim with pinned-capacity on our staging GPUs, not the Nimbus-dedicated pool. We should run the same workload on your dedicated pool to get accurate p95 numbers.

[10:25] Jordan: Ok next, quantization failure modes — Priya mentioned numerical instability on long-context. What mitigation options do we have?
[10:34] Priya: A few: selective layer-wise fallback (keep first/last layers in higher precision), per-token dynamic scaling, and hybrid quantization where we quantize only attention projections but leave layernorm and softmax in FP16. That reduces perf but fixes some coherence issues.
[10:58] Carlos: Any quick wins?
[11:02] Priya: Layer-wise selective quant is the fastest to test and often solves the worst tails. Also a heavier calibration dataset helps the quantizer pick better scales.

[12:30] Aisha: On the security side, we need to confirm KMS integration and audit log retention for the dedicated deployment. Jordan, last week you said Redwood Optmize and Redwood Dedicated support KMS — can you resend the doc?
[12:45] Jordan: Yep I'll share the security pack and the KMS integration notes. We call out HSM options in the pack. Also note that the private deployment has a slightly different audit schema, I'll include both.

[14:00] Mei: Quick question about model rollouts — if we decide to A/B test FP8 vs INT8 in production, can Redwood handle per-route routing and automatic fallback?
[14:12] Priya: Yes, our routing can do per-route traffic splits and auto-fallback to FP16 or a safer variant if error rates increase. There is some instrumentation setup required — we can push metrics into your Grafana via traces.

[16:05] Carlos: Back to numbers, can you remind me of cost delta? Int8 was ~35% cost reduction vs FP16 and FP8 was around 28%?
[16:15] Priya: Correct for token compute costs. INT8 tends to give the biggest cost win. But remember operational complexity — more fallbacks means you might need to pay for slightly more headroom.

[18:00] Samir: Network question: if we move to dedicated in our VPC, we need to schedule peering and have maintenance windows. What is Redwood's recommended schedule?
[18:08] Jordan: We usually suggest a short maintenance window with pre-provisioned pools. Samir, maybe send your peering windows and we'll align.

[20:00] Priya: I want to call out a couple of specific prompt types: transactional confirmations and multi-turn support chats — those are where INT8 shows the biggest regressions. If those are critical, I'd recommend hybrid quant or mixing FP8 for those routes.

[22:40] Aisha: Can we do a small canary? Route 5% of traffic to INT8 on non-critical accounts and monitor token-level quality?

[22:50] Jordan: Yes, we can set that up. Priya will help configure monitoring thresholds and alerting.

[24:30] Priya: About the calibration dataset — Carlos please share the 500-1k representative prompts. That will help lower the outlier regressions.
[24:40] Carlos: Will do by end of day tomorrow.

[26:00] Jordan: Action recap: Jordan to share consolidated benchmark sheet and security pack; Priya to run 95p latency on dedicated pool; Carlos to send prompts; Samir to confirm peering windows. Anything else?

[26:30] Mei: One more, can you also include a short runbook for fallback configuration so our SREs can understand the rollback steps?

[26:40] Jordan: Yup, we'll include a runbook with the benchmark.

[28:00] Priya: A quick note — FP8 stability in our runtime is improving; some of the kernel fallback behavior is due to an edge-case of rotary positional encoding scaling we hit in a small subset of sequences. We have a patch in the next runtime build that reduces those fallbacks, but we should retest once it's deployed.

[30:10] Carlos: Good to know. When's that patch dropping?
[30:14] Priya: Tentative 2026-06-08, if tests go green. We'll ping you.

[32:00] Aisha: From a business perspective, we prefer INT8 if it meets QA criteria because of the cost delta, but we need guarantees for the tail. If hybrid is required for only 5-10% of routes that's acceptable.

[33:00] Jordan: Ok, so plan: run dedicated perf tests, run hybrid experiments on the 5 flagged prompts, and align on thresholds. We'll prepare a short decision matrix for next week.

[35:20] Priya: I'll also include per-prompt diffs in the sheet — color-coded and with sample outputs so you can eyeball where the quality regresses.

[36:40] Samir: One operational ask — can Redwood export GPU trace logs in the same format we use for our infra so our SREs can ingest them?

[36:50] Priya: Yep we can export logs and we have a small adapter script. Jordan will attach the script to the benchmark upload.

[38:30] Jordan: Any competitive notes? Did anyone test Anthropic or Vertex on these prompts?

[38:40] Carlos: We ran a quick comparison last month; Anthropic had better short-context coherence but cost was higher. Not a formal head-to-head in this run.

[40:00] Mei: Ok, timeline — if we get the dedicated p95 numbers and prompts this week, we can decide by next Wednesday whether to start a 2-week canary.

[41:00] Jordan: Great. I'll send meeting notes, attach the benchmark CSV and the security pack, and schedule the next sync for 2026-06-09.

[43:10] Aisha: Thanks everyone, appreciate the work.

[43:20] Carlos: Thanks.

[43:30] Priya: Thanks, we'll follow up.

[44:00] Meeting end.

References:
- Benchmark spreadsheet (drive link): https://drive.redwood.example/nimbus-quant-bench-20260602
- Security pack (drive link): https://drive.redwood.example/security-pack-nimbus-20260602
- Raw logs: https://drive.redwood.example/nimbus-logs-20260602

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription had minor errors (K-V cache spelled K-V cash; Redwood Optimize as Redwood Optmize), occasional speaker label swaps around 02:00-03:00.
